$comment: BC Transit's East Kootenay system (export 21 on https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/, checked 2026-11-27): Cranbrook, Kimberley, the Columbia Valley (Invermere) and the Elk Valley (Fernie, Sparwood, Elkford). Its own feed because it's in Alberta's time zone, unlike the West Kootenay and Creston (config/feeds/bc-transit-kootenays/). One agency; route_ids end in -EKT. 13 routes. Every route is drawn; overrides and exclusions: routes.json. Terms: https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/terms-of-use/ (identify BC Transit as the source; no use of its marks).
name: BC Transit (East Kootenay)
$timezone: Its export's agency_timezone (checked 2026-11-27): the East Kootenay keeps Mountain Time, as Alberta does.
$timezoneChecks: Known facts about the feed's time zone that the runtime's time zone data (tzdata, via ICU) must agree with; the server refuses to start otherwise (checkTimezoneData in packages/transit-core/src/time.ts). Times are still always computed from the runtime's data, never from these. Alberta stayed on UTC-6 from 2026-11-01 (tzdata 2026e has America/Edmonton at UTC-6 all year; issue #261); older data falls back to UTC-7 that day.

static.$comment: Regenerated daily with a new feed_version (e.g. "202611270/20261126 21:00:00/20261127 04:00:00") even when the timetable is unchanged, so fetch-gtfs archives a version only when its files differ from the newest archived one. No dated history. Uses calendar_dates.txt only (no calendar.txt), shape_dist_traveled in metres. How often the timetable really changes: OPEN-QUESTIONS #1.

realtime.$comment: No API key and no stated request limit (answers for operatorIds=21 checked 2026-11-27). Polled within a modest budget: OPEN-QUESTIONS #2.
realtime.$poll: Positions and trip updates every 5 minutes while buses run (05:00-24:00), every 10 overnight; alerts every 15 minutes: small systems, where frequent polling isn't needed (as for the West Kootenay: Braden MacDonald, 2026-11-02; config/operators/bc-transit/operator.json). About 610 requests a day; dailyCap is a safety net. OPEN-QUESTIONS #2.
realtime.$staleGraceS: Clients fall back to schedule estimates once live data is this much older than the positions poll interval: one missed 5-minute poll (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$coverageSlackS: Recorder coverage breaks when snapshots are further apart than the positions poll interval plus this (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$interpolateSlackS: Interpolate between two fixes at most the positions poll interval plus this apart: across one missed 5-minute poll (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$extrapolateSlackS: Predict a bus forward for at most the positions poll interval plus this (BC Transit's fixes are fresh when fetched, under 30 s old elsewhere; guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).

display.$tripId: Trip ids are three internal ids, <journey>:<variant>:<block> (e.g. 2102626:14622067:14634975); the journey alone is unique on any date, as in BC Transit's other feeds.
display.$feedVersion: Versions look like "202611020/20261101 21:00:00/20261102 03:00:00": the export date and a sequence number, then the export window. A merged feed takes the newest of its exports'.
